label: Black Forest Labs (FLUX)
terms_note: Pay-as-you-go credits (non-refundable), commercial use of outputs allowed, BFL may train on inputs/outputs, no re-hosting of the models as an endpoint, usage policy must be enforced downstream; 24 active tasks per key (kontext-max 6) -> 429, 402 = no credits, result URLs expire after 10 min

auth: 1. Tenant creates an account at bfl.ai → organisation → project → **API key** (dashboard), buys credits (pay-as-you-go, 1 credit = $0.01, non-refundable).
2. Header `x-key: <key>` on every call. Keys do not expire.
3. Verify: `GET /v1/credits` → remaining balance (our current probe `GET /v1/get_result?id=<random>` works but the credits call is the documented one and also feeds a low-balance warning).
4. MCP: `https://mcp.bfl.ai` — OAuth sign-in with the BFL account, pick the org that pays; no key copied.

reference.limits: **24 active tasks per API key** (flux-kontext-max: 6) → HTTP 429 until a task finishes; exponential back-off. 402 = insufficient credits. 422 = bad body (e.g. `safety_tolerance` above an endpoint's max). Poll at ~0.5–1 s. Result URLs expire after 10 minutes and must not be served to end users — download and re-host. FLUX API Service Terms: outputs may be used commercially in the developer's applications; developer may **not** re-host the models as an API endpoint or resell raw API access; must enforce the FLUX Usage Policy downstream (content screening); BFL may use inputs + outputs to improv

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: BFL API key (bfl.ai dashboard > organisation > project > API keys), sent as the x-key header. Requests spend pay-as-you-go credits (1 credit = $0.01).

config_fields.name: webhook_url
config_fields.help: Optional HTTPS URL that BFL POSTs finished results to (webhook_url on every generation request); the way to receive results, since polling needs the per-task polling_url.

adapter.terms: FLUX API Service Terms: outputs may be used commercially; do not re-host the models as an endpoint; enforce the FLUX usage policy downstream. Result URLs expire after 10 minutes and must be downloaded and re-served, not shown to end users directly.

me.note: GET /v1/credits -> {credits}: the remaining credit balance of the key's organisation (there is no user endpoint).

generate_image.note: POST /v1/{model} (default flux-kontext-pro; also flux-kontext-max, flux-2-pro, flux-2-max, flux-2-flex, flux-pro-1.1, flux-pro-1.1-ultra …) with {prompt, input_image (URL or base64, for edits), seed, aspect_ratio (21:9…9:21)} -> {id, polling_url, cost}. Generation is asynchronous: the finished image URL (result.sample) is delivered to the configured webhook_url or read from raw.polling_url with the x-key header. FLUX.2 models size with width/height instead of aspect_ratio. negative_prompt and size are not sent.

generate_video.note: POST /v1/flux-3-video {mode: t2v, prompt, aspect_ratio (21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 … or auto), duration (5–20 s)} -> {id, polling_url}: text-to-video with native audio. Image-to-video (mode i2v) needs a keyframes array and is not mapped; image_url and model are not sent. Results are fetched from raw.polling_url: webhook_url is not sent, because every Flux 3 video input schema in https://api.bfl.ai/openapi.json (Flux3VideoT2VInputs …) forbids extra properties and has no webhook_url (FluxKontextProInputs, used by generate_image, does; auth audit 2026-09-26).

not_offered.get_job: Results must be polled at the per-task `polling_url`: 'When using the primary global endpoint (api.bfl.ai) or regional endpoints (api.eu.bfl.ai, api.us.bfl.ai), you must use the polling_url returned in the initial request response' (https://docs.bfl.ai/api_integration/integration_guidelines). That URL's host is a per-task cluster, and the runtime does not send credentials to a host taken from a response or an argument (needs a response-URL follow with a host allow-list); use the webhook_url config field instead.
not_offered.list_items: No content-item resource; the only listings are fine-tunes (GET /v1/my_finetunes, ids only).
not_offered.delete_item: No content-item resource (POST /v1/delete_finetune deletes a fine-tune, which this vocabulary does not model).

evidence: host api.bfl.ai: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (DigiCert Inc)
probe: 3/3 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
spec https://api.bfl.ai/openapi.json: 3/3 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
auth_audit.notes: Fixed: generate_video no longer sends webhook_url, which the Flux 3 video input schemas forbid (additionalProperties false).
